title: Profile menus and the duplicate client cabinet
why: `S-048` and `S-111` are one compiled profile sheet shipped in two bundles — `сайт и приложение/app.html` L39541-39611 and `maya-os-site/index.html` L36496-36564, the same four rows and the same role branch — not two separate menus. It holds cabinet entry, settings, theme and logout, and `S-111` is a tab with no screen: the 4th client tab does nothing but open the sheet, whose «Личный кабинет» row already duplicates the «Кабинет» tab two positions to its left. `S-176` is different in kind. It is an independent client-cabinet implementation living inside the marketing page and calling the same production endpoints as the PWA (`cabinet_session`, `cabinet_me_login`), so retiring it removes a duplicate client app, not a menu. It does not by itself deliver one client surface: those endpoints are called from three bundles (app.html L40124/40130/40136, `сайт и приложение/index.html` L5592-5593, `maya-os-site/index.html` L37031/37037), and this group retires only the marketing overlay — two implementations remain for a later package. Its re-parenting to `<body>` is deliberate and load-bearing: `#promo-overlay` (L4307) is left unclosed and carries `display:none`, so it swallows the tail of `<body>` and anything nested there never renders. The defect to fix is the unclosed overlay, not the workaround.
disappear: The profile sheet in both bundles, the 4th tab that exists only to open it, and the marketing-page overlay as a separate client codebase. Its own mechanics go with it: the body scroll lock, and the `?cab_demo=1|needphone|guest|login|wait` QA harness that auto-opens the cabinet and force-hides the splash (L5824-5827). The body re-parenting disappears only after the unclosed `#promo-overlay` is fixed, or once the surface no longer renders inside that page — removed any earlier, the merged surface renders invisible.
remain: Everything these rows front: cabinet entry, settings, logout, and the client's own points, visits and history behind the same authenticated endpoints, with one of the three implementations that call them removed. Dark/light theme — and here the successor should better today rather than copy it: the present toggle deliberately does not persist (`__meSetDark`, L38412) and `__meThemeTick` reverts a manual choice every five minutes and on every focus change, so theme belongs in settings as a setting that sticks. The RU/EN bilingual re-render hooked into `window.setLanguage` — 12 occurrences in the site page, none in the PWA — so a site-language contract has to exist before the site entry retires. The no-`fetch`/no-`Promise` fallback that redirects to `/app/` (L5768), today the only graceful degradation for browsers lacking them; drop it and none remains.
risk: MEDIUM — one loss is unambiguous and the rest are narrower than they look. In `S-048`, `__meGo('settings')` occurs exactly once in the file (L39558) and is the only route to the settings screen: reminder timing, per-event notification switches, promo frequency, quiet hours. Lose that row without a replacement and a client keeps a consent record with no live control over what is sent to them — the one loss that touches the 152-ФЗ contour, and on its own enough to carry MEDIUM. The logout row is the only sign-out for a non-business client: business roles keep «Выйти из аккаунта» and «Выйти на всех устройствах» in the cabinet's «Сессии» tab (L14496-14518) and «Выйти из учётной записи» in the owner panel (L34761), besides the access-compat screen (L38543) — and in every case what is at stake is the button, not server-side revocation, which is untouched. `S-176` is not the only zero-install account path: `/app/` is itself zero-install, and the marketing page both links it and hard-falls back to it (L5768); a desktop visitor loses the one-click in-page cabinet from the site nav (L656), the RU/EN re-render and the QA harness — not their points, visits and history. `S-111` holds the only entry to theme control, but that control does not persist today. The role-aware «Личный кабинет» routing (staff → mystat, manager → default tab, legacy → cabinet) picks a destination rather than granting a permission, but it may not be dropped on the assumption that the destination guards itself: these three rows carry no backend evidence at all, and the cabinet's own tab list repeats the same client-side test (`viewManager`, `saasIsStaffRole()`, `saasIsCalManager()`, L13960-13982). Resolve the destination server-side and confirm its data endpoints authorise independently before the branch goes. All three rows are RETIRE AFTER PARITY (K16), so the hazard is a parity failure at the moment of retirement, not a live one.
user_impact: Two populations feel this, and the group is smaller than it looks: S-048 and S-111 are the SAME compiled profile sheet in two bundles — `сайт и приложение/app.html` L39541-39611 and `maya-os-site/index.html` L36496-36564, the same four rows and the same role branch — so a client tapping the 4th «Профиль» tab (CLIENT_TABS L5864: Запись · Чат · Кабинет · Профиль) and a staff member tapping the avatar in the staff-home header (L29081 — an avatar button, not a «Кабинет» tile) open one component, not two; the sheet's «Личный кабинет» row already duplicates the «Кабинет» tab two positions to its left. One loss is verified and material: `__meGo('settings')` occurs exactly once in app.html (L39558) and is the only route to `ASettings` (L25564) — reminder timing, per-event notification switches, «Акции и промокоды» frequency, quiet hours; lose the row and a client keeps the consent record with no live control over what is sent. The logout claim must be narrowed: that row is the only sign-out **for a non-business client**, because under `viewBusiness` the cabinet's «Сессии» tab carries «Выйти из аккаунта» and «Выйти на всех устройствах» (L14496-14518) and `ASaasOwnerPanel` carries «Выйти из учётной записи» (L34761), besides AccessCompatScreen (L38543). The S-176 claim is too strong: `/app/` is itself zero-install, index.html links it three times and hard-falls back to it at L5768 `if(!CAN){location.href='/app/'}`; what a desktop visitor actually loses is the one-click in-page cabinet from the marketing nav (L656), the RU/EN re-render (`setLanguage` 12 hits in index.html, 0 in app.html) and the `?cab_demo=` QA harness. Theme is the one clear gain, not a like-for-like move: `__meSetDark` explicitly does not persist ("тема автоматическая — не персистим выбор", L38410) and `__meThemeTick` reverts the manual toggle on a 5-minute interval and on every focus/visibilitychange, so today's row is a toggle that does not stick.
security_impact: Neutral for authority — no hole is closed and none is opened — and the claimed improvement does not survive counting. The role branch the RISK line names is correctly described as a destination chooser rather than a gate: `_pmSaasRole` is `meSaasCurrentRole()` → `bundle.user.role` out of the stored server-issued bundle, and it only picks which cabinet tab opens. But the inference drawn from that — that the screens it opens enforce their own access, so removing it needs no server-side check — is evidenced nowhere in S-048/S-111/S-176, which carry no backend evidence at all, and the visible destination repeats the same client-side test: the cabinet's tab list itself branches on `viewManager`, `saasIsStaffRole()` and `saasIsCalManager()` (app.html L13960-13982). The RISK line therefore stands as written — resolve the destination server-side AND confirm the destination's data endpoints authorize independently before dropping the branch; it may not be booked as already true. The consolidation improvement is miscounted: `cabinet_session` / `cabinet_me_login` are called from three bundles, not two (app.html L40124/40130/40136, `сайт и приложение/index.html` L5592-5593, `maya-os-site/index.html` L37031/37037), and G10 retires only the marketing overlay, leaving two client-cabinet implementations. It is also not a storage or attack-surface reduction: index.html and app.html share one origin and both read and write `web_session_token` in localStorage, so the token stays exactly where it was. Under frozen limitation 7 — Gate 10 is a shadow gate, "three front doors, one function" is measured, not enforced — this is a measurement, not a delivered control. Nothing here touches consent records, tenant isolation, STEP_UP (unreachable) or approval role-gating. The one regression is narrower than stated: dropping S-048's logout row removes the only sign-out affordance for a non-business client (business roles keep the cabinet «Сессии» tab and the owner panel), and it is an affordance loss only — server-side revocation and the multi-device revoke path are untouched.
